headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Flowise’s broad network/files access can expose or operationalize outputs from a non-runnable awesome-nlp list, while shared-state orchestration raises conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while agent_b has files and browser/network tools but no shared channel with agent_a. Without a direct ingestion path, injection via agent_a into agent_b is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF agent_a becomes runnable and emits untrusted content that agent_b parses as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any automatic import of agent_a outputs into agent_b flows.
Add provenance labels to any copied content.
Review any future bridge for instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read/write files and use broad network egress, so if it is pointed at sensitive chatflow inputs or uploaded files, those contents can leave the environment. agent_a touches no data and has no egress, so the main leakage path is one-way through agent_b, not from agent_a.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into agent_b flows, those contents may be sent to external model providers or HTTP tools.
IF agent_a is later given data-bearing inputs, any copied outputs into agent_b inherit the same exposure path.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive test data.
Remove or disable external HTTP/search tools in production flows.
Use a separate workspace for uploaded files.
Rotate any exposed tool credentials.
Add a manual review step before networked actions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multiple instances with shared state via server datastore and can write files, so concurrent runs can conflict on mutable resources. agent_a has no write or runtime surface, so it does not add conflict itself; the pair risk comes from agent_b’s shared-state concurrency model.
conditions: IF multiple Flowise instances operate on the same datastore or filesystem, write conflicts become possible.
IF agent_a is later wrapped to generate files consumed by agent_b, stale-write races may appear.
mitigations: Serialize writes to shared resources.
Use per-run directories for outputs.
Disable concurrent edits to the same flow artifacts.
Snapshot the datastore before bulk changes.
Add locking around any shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as tool inputs, so if agent_a’s content is copied into a flow, errors can cascade without verification. agent_a itself is only an awesome-list and cannot act, but its outputs could still be rendered or operationalized by agent_b if manually bridged.
conditions: IF agent_a content is imported into a Flowise node without validation, downstream actions may rely on it as authoritative.
IF agent_b is configured to send emails, API calls, or browser actions from that content, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a verification node before any action-taking step.
Require human approval for external side effects.
Mark imported content as untrusted.
Limit flows to read-only summarization until reviewed.
Add tests for malformed or stale upstream content.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. agent_b handles chatflow inputs/outputs and may store files, while agent_a has no data classes touched, so compliance exposure is limited to deployment choices rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_b in a deployment without the required controls, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF agent_b is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules than the surrounding system, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Confirm deployment region and data-processing terms.
Disable file uploads for sensitive workflows.
Review logs for accidental inclusion of personal data.
